title: Dominic and the Inventory
premise: Ivo Amberdale has spent twenty years cataloguing silences in a night library, including the one surrounding the fire that killed their father and freed their brother Dominic from a family that never fit him. When the childhood house on Amberdale Lane goes to auction, Ivo discovers their mother's will names them co-inheritor with Dominic—forcing a reunion neither wants. Returning home, Ivo uncovers evidence that the fire was no accident and that Dominic took the blame for someone else. In the end, Ivo must choose between protecting the family's fragile peace and testifying to what they saw as a child, trading inheritance and loyalty for a truth that finally lets both siblings be free.
about_author: Jude Oyelaran is a former archivist who writes novels about the things families file away and forget. They live between two cities and keep, by their own admission, too many unfinished notebooks.

chapters.title: The Night Shift
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. We meet Ivo among the sleeping library's shelves, reshelving returned books and recording in a private ledger the things patrons almost say. A letter arrives: the Amberdale house is up for auction, and Ivo is named in the will. The beat is quiet dread—the inventory of unsaid things is about to be opened.

chapters.title: What the Will Says
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the solicitor's office, Ivo learns they share the inheritance with Dominic, estranged since the fire twenty years ago and recently released from prison. The solicitor hints the mother left conditions. Ivo refuses at first, then finds a note in their mother's handwriting: 'Ask Ivo. Ivo saw.' The beat: guilt rekindled into obligation.

chapters.title: Amberdale Lane
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo returns to the shuttered house, walking rooms frozen since childhood, and finds the mother's own inventory—a box of clippings, photographs, and a scorched key. A neighbor, Mrs. Okonkwo, watches from her porch and says only, 'You were there that night.' The beat: the past asserting itself physically.

chapters.title: Dominic
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic works nights at a freight depot, keeping his head down, when Ivo appears asking about the fire. He deflects with jokes and anger but agrees to meet once—for the house money, he claims. Alone, he burns an old letter addressed to Ivo. The beat: guarded tenderness curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Back in the city, Ivo rereads their childhood diary and realizes fragments don't match the official story: the fire started before Dominic's shift ended, and someone else's car was on the lane. Ivo begins cross-referencing like a catalogue. The beat: the librarian's precision becoming an instrument of investigation.

chapters.title: Mrs. Okonkwo's Testimony
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Mrs. Okonkwo tells Ivo what she saw but never reported: Uncle Ray's truck leaving the lane minutes after the flames rose, and the mother paying her silence with groceries and threats. She gives Ivo the scorched key's twin. The beat: complicity revealed—everyone kept the inventory, not just Ivo.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the auction, Uncle Ray appears as a bidder, confident and generous, buying back the house cheap while charming the town. Ivo confronts him privately; Ray reminds Ivo that testimony from a traumatized child means nothing now, and that Dominic confessed. The beat: rising tension—justice outside the law starts to look impossible inside it.

chapters.title: What Dominic Took
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Cornered by Ivo's evidence, Dominic finally confesses why he pleaded guilty: Ray threatened to reveal that the mother knew and did nothing, destroying what was left of the family. Dominic chose to be the villain so Ivo could stay innocent. The beat: the climax of loyalty vs. truth—love expressed as a lie.

chapters.title: Fire, Retold
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo reconstructs the night fully: Ray set the fire over the inheritance, the mother covered for her brother, and Dominic absorbed the blame. Ivo takes the evidence—a signed statement from Mrs. Okonkwo, the key, the ledger—to a retired detective who owes the family nothing and owes the truth everything. The beat: decisive turn toward justice.

chapters.title: Everything Said
chapters.summary: Split final chapter. Ray is charged; the auction sale collapses; the house is sold to fund Dominic's appeal, which succeeds. On the empty lawn, Ivo and Dominic read their mother's last page aloud together and burn the ledger of unsaid things. Ivo returns to the night library changed—now keeping an inventory of things finally said. The beat: grief transmuted into freedom.
